title: Ontario Summer Games grant and 2026 borrowing
subtitle: Temporary borrowing bylaws, municipal benchmarking results for 2024, and a question on accessibility measures
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council give $250,000 from the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve to Explore Waterloo Region to host the 2026 Ontario Summer Games in July 2026 {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the reserve can cover the grant and still hold a healthy balance. They expect thousands of athletes plus visiting family and friends, which would bring hotel stays and economic benefit to the region.

The committee also recommended that Council authorize the Chief Financial Officer, by bylaw, to borrow funds in 2026 on a temporary basis to meet operating and capital needs. This was passed as part of the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}.

The committee received the 2024 MBNCanada performance measurement report for information. It shows the region performing well in most service areas, with strong results in accounts payable, higher shelter capacity, and cost pressures in the vehicle fleet from aging vehicles. No delegations or presentations from the public took place. The next committee meeting is on January 13, 2026.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended supporting Explore Waterloo Region's hosting of the 2026 Ontario Summer Games in July 2026 with a $250,000 grant from the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve.
The committee recommended authorizing the Chief Financial Officer, by bylaw, to borrow funds in 2026 as needed on a temporary basis for operating and capital expenditures.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, including the temporary borrowing report.

debate: Staff said the grant is affordable because the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve has enough funds and would still hold a substantial balance afterward.
Staff pointed to the economic case: roughly 4,000 participants housed mainly at universities, plus additional visiting family and friends who would stay in hotels.
One councillor asked whether the accommodation tax applies to university dorm stays; staff said they did not believe it does.

On the benchmarking report, one councillor noted the fleet results and the region's reported high staff turnover, and asked why there were no equity, inclusion or accessibility measures, citing the earlier transit accessibility discussion.
Staff replied that the accessibility point is useful feedback they can pass to MBNCanada to consider for future measures.
